item.title: Non-comparable invariant metrics and failure of Gromov hyperbolicity on a real-analytic pseudoconvex domain
item.description: arXiv:2610.36124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the explicit bounded pseudoconvex domain \[ \Omega=\{(z_1,z_2,w)\in\mathbb C^3: |w|^2+|z_1z_2(z_1-z_2)|^2+|z_1|^8+|z_2|^8<1\}. \] Its boundary is real analytic and has finite D'Angelo type everywhere. We prove two assertions about the invariant metrics of this domain. First, $(\Omega,k_\Omega)$ is not Gromov hyperbolic; in fact arbitrarily fat Kobayashi geodesic triangles occur in every neighborhood of the type-$8$ point $(0,0,1)$. Second, the Carath\'eodory--Reiffen and Kobayashi--Royden metrics are not uniformly comparable. Along an explicit family of tangential directions the Carath\'eodory metric tends to zero while the Kobayashi metric has a positive limit. For the corresponding distances there are points $x_j,y_j\to(0,0,1)$ such that $c_\Omega(x_j,y_j)\to0$ while $k_\Omega(x_j,y_j)\to\infty$. This gives, among bounded real-analytic pseudoconvex domains, an affirmative answer to Problem~7.3.2 of the Several Complex Variables Problem List.
item.dc:creator: Armen Edigarian

item.title: From boundary geometry to counterexamples in Smale's mean value problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.36158v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper provides a human digestion of the recent counterexample to Smale's mean value problem found by GPT-6 Astra. We give a geometric mechanism for constructing counterexamples. An outward normal that re-enters an analytic Jordan domain, subject to a curvature condition, yields a holomorphic model whose normalized divided differences exceed one in modulus on the boundary. Polynomial perturbations then concentrate every critical point near the boundary whilst preserving the strict inequality. This turns boundary geometry into counterexamples in every sufficiently large degree. We also locate these critical points to first order and show that their limiting distribution is the logarithmic equilibrium measure on the boundary. We end with an explicit example of degree $29\,984$, verified by interval arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Tom Adamczewski, Matthew J. Colbrook

item.title: The inverse Monge--Amp\`ere flow on klt Fano varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.36414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the long time existence of the inverse Monge--Amp\`ere flow on a klt $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano variety $X$. We further prove that $X$ admits a K\"ahler--Einstein metric if and only if the flow converges in $L^1$.
item.dc:creator: Jianchun Chu, Tam\'as Darvas, Yaxiong Liu

item.title: Different approach to certain problems in univalent function theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.36737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using different approach we consider some problems for the class $\mathcal{S}_{ex}^{\star}$ defined by the condition $\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}\prec e^{\alpha z}$, $0<\alpha\leq1.$ Our method is more simple than that used by Das and Sarkar in their work: \textit{Sharp coefficient estimates for the exponential starlike class $S^\star_{ex}$} (\cite{DS26}).
item.dc:creator: Milutin Obradovi\'{c}, Nikola Tuneski

item.title: Essential norms of fractional Volterra-type operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.37548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a radial doubling weight $\mu$ on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ and $f(z)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty \hat{f}(n)z^n\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$, the fractional derivative of $f$ induced by $\mu$ is $$ D^\mu(f)(z) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{\hat{f}(n)}{\mu_{2n+1}}z^n, $$ where $\mu_{2n+1}=\int_0^1 r^{2n+1}\mu(r)\,dr$ are the odd moments of $\mu$. The fractional integral of $f$ induced by $\mu$ is $I^\mu(f)(z)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty \mu_{2n+1}\hat{f}(n)z^n$. We study the fractional Volterra-type operator $$ V_{\mu,g}(f)(z)=I^\mu(f\cdot D^\mu(g))(z),\quad f\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D}), $$ with symbol $g\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$, introduced by Bellavita, Moreno, Nikolaidis and Pel\'aez. First, we estimate the essential norm of $V_{\mu,g}$ acting on $H^p$ and $A^p_\alpha$. Later, we study the same questions for $V_{\mu,g}:H^p\to H^q$ and $V_{\mu,g}:A^p_\alpha\to A^q_\alpha$, characterizing their boundedness and compactness and estimating their essential norms for all $0<p,q<\infty$.
item.dc:creator: \'Alvaro Miguel Moreno

item.title: Vanishing theorems for $L^2$ Dolbeault cohomology groups of projective Hartogs triangles
item.description: arXiv:2610.37572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, using J.-P. Demailly's $L^2$ existence theorem for possibly incomplete K\"ahler metrics, we establish $L^2$ estimates and vanishing theorems for a class of domains in $\mathbb P^n$ without any boundary regularity assumptions. In particular, we give an affirmative answer to M.-C. Shaw's question concerning the vanishing of the $L^2$ Dolbeault cohomology groups of projective Hartogs triangles.
item.dc:creator: Jian Chen

item.title: A functional model for hyponormal contractions
item.description: arXiv:2610.35880v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish an analytical model for a class of hyponormal contractions $T$ satisfying $Ran[T^*,T] \subseteq \mathcal D_{T^*}\ominus \mathcal D_T$, where $\mathcal D_{T^*}$ and $\mathcal D_T$ are the associated defect spaces for $T$. We also show that, under a certain condition, a contraction $T$ with $\mathcal D_T \subseteq \mathcal D_{T^*}$ is hyponormal.
item.dc:creator: Amit Maji, Sachin Paramanik

item.title: Algebraic properties of Truncated Toeplitz $+$ Truncated Hankel operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.35897v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the algebraic properties of $\mathcal{S}_\theta$---the class of truncated Toeplitz plus truncated Hankel operators --- on the model space $\mathcal{K}_\theta$. We also give a complete characterization of the intersection class of truncated Toeplitz and truncated Hankel operators under certain conditions. As applications, we describe the non-uniqueness of a decomposition $T=A+B$, show that self-adjoint operators admit self-adjoint decompositions, give a necessary and sufficient inclusion criterion for $\mathcal{S}_\theta$ when $\theta$ is a finite Blaschke product, and, from a first-order commutator characterization of $\mathcal{S}_\theta$, describe the products of its elements and the operators commuting with $S_\theta+ S_\theta^{*}$.
item.dc:creator: Kritika Babbar, Satyabrata Majee, Amit Maji

item.title: Boundary and Interior of Root Sets of Power Series
item.description: arXiv:2610.36279v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study the set $\mathcal{M}_M$ of roots of power series with coefficients in $\{0, \pm 1, ..., \pm M \}$ and constant coefficient $1$. We prove that every nonreal root in the unit disk of a polynomial of this form is an interior point of $\mathcal{M}_M$. Moreover we establish a dimension formula and show the corresponding Hausdorff measure is finite and positive for a family of attractors parameterized by boundary parameters $\lambda \in \partial \mathcal{M}_M \setminus \mathbb{R}$. Finally we show that $\partial \mathcal{M}_M$ has Lebesgue measure zero.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Kewarth

item.title: Outer Lipschitz Geometry of Unions of Tangential Nodal Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.36381v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In 2000, Birbrair and Fernandes proved that the H\"older Semicomplex of the branches of a germ of a curve with its contact orders is a complete invariant of outer bi-Lipschitz equivalence of definable sets in polynomially bounded o-minimal structures. They also proved a realization theorem for it, i.e., for each H\"older semicomplex $G$, there is a germ of a semialgebraic curve $(X,x_0)$ such that the H\"older Semicomplex of $(X,x_0)$ coincides with $G$. In 2000, Birbrair proposed the problem of finding and characterizing all the H\"older semicomplexes that can be realized as a H\"older Semicomplex of a real analytic curve. Solving this problem in its full generality is a notoriously hard task; however, in this paper, we provide a complete answer to this problem when we restrict it to tangential nodal curves: curves defined as the union of the zero set of a harmonic function and its tangent cone at a fixed point.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Edson Sampaio, Luan Moura Sousa, Emanoel Ferreira de Souza

item.title: Arithmetic Poisson summation formulas
item.description: arXiv:2610.36606v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate Poisson summation with periodic weights in forms adapted to arithmetic sums (arithmetic Poisson summation formulas, APSF), in scalar, polynomial-congruence and vector-divisibility versions, extending Berndt's arithmetic Poisson formula. We use APSF as a common framework to rederive Ramanujan's formula for $\zeta(2m+1)$ and its character analogues due to Katayama and Berndt-Straub, the functional equations of $\zeta$, of Dirichlet's beta function and of Estermann's function, and the exponents of Tolev and Chen-Wang for power-free values of $x^2+y^2+1$ and $x^2+y^2+z^2+k$. It also gives reciprocity laws with Kelvin-function kernels for Lambert series twisted by a Dirichlet character over imaginary quadratic fields of arbitrary class number; asymptotic formulas with error terms for $r$-free values of $x_1^2+\cdots+x_n^2+k$, with Gaussian-weighted versions and the meromorphic continuation of the associated Dirichlet series; an argument of Terras, relating two-dimensional Bessel series for all odd zeta values and even Dirichlet beta values; and a Gaussian representation of a Mersenne-Fermat prime detector.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Panzone, Lucas Oliveira

item.title: A characterization of equality between de Branges--Rovnyak and Dirichlet spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.36943v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize when a de Branges--Rovnyak space coincides with a harmonically weighted Dirichlet space. We obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for this identification, which settles a long-standing open problem. We illustrate the result with several examples, that include measures supported on uncountable sets.
item.dc:creator: Carlo Bellavita, Eugenio Dellepiane, Shuaibing Luo

item.title: The Beurling-type theorem for powers of weighted Bergman shifts
item.description: arXiv:2610.37035v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{B}_{\alpha}$ denote the shift operator on the weighted Bergman space $A^2_\alpha(\mathbb{D})$. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, the Beurling-type theorem holds for $\mathcal{B}_{\alpha}^k$ on $A^2_\alpha(\mathbb{D})$ if and only if $-1<\alpha\leq1$. We also show that, for every $\alpha>-1$, there exists a finite Blaschke product $B$ such that $M_{B}$ admits a cyclic invariant subspace but fails the wandering subspace property.
item.dc:creator: Shibo Xu, Tao Yu

item.title: Polynomial automorphisms of C^2 with the same equilibrium measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.37600v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We review the following question: when do two polynomial automorphisms of C^2 have the same maximal entropy measure? While the answer has been known for some time when both automorphisms are compositions of H\'enon maps, the general case is more delicate. In this (mostly expository) note we explain how recent results in random dynamics give an almost complete solution to the question, and point out a number of related open problems.
item.dc:creator: Romain Dujardin

item.title: On quaternionic analysis and a certain generalized fractal-fractional $\psi$-Fueter operator
item.description: arXiv:2502.15518v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper introduces a fractal $\psi$-Fueter operator in the quaternionic context inspired by the concepts of proportional derivative and Hausdorff derivative ({fractal derivative}) of a function with respect to a fractal measure. Moreover, we establish the corresponding Stokes and Borel-Pompeiu formulas associated to this generalized fractal $\psi$-Fueter operator with respect to a vector valued function induced by truncated exponential functions.
item.dc:creator: Juan Adri\'an Ram\'irez-Belman, Jos\'e Oscar Gonz\'alez-Cervantes, Juan Bory-Reyes

item.title: On the distribution kernels of Toeplitz operators on CR manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2512.16506v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the distribution kernel of a Toeplitz operator associated with a classical pseudodifferential operator on a compact, embeddable, strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold. The main result consists of a formula for the values at the diagonal of the second coefficient in the expansion of the symbol of the kernel. We also establish asymptotic expansions for Toeplitz operators on the positive part of a compact not necessary strictly pseudoconvex CR orbifold under certain natural assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Chin-Yu Hsiao, Ood Shabtai

item.title: Radii of Starlikeness of Spirallike Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.06175v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A normalized analytic function $f$ defined on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ is called $\alpha$-spirallike if $f(\mathbb{D})$ is an $\alpha$-spirallike domain, that is, for every $z\in f(\mathbb{D})$, the $\alpha$-spiral $ze^{-e^{i\alpha}t}$, $t\ge0$, is contained in $f(\mathbb{D})$, or equivalently, if $\operatorname{Re}\!\left(e^{i\alpha} {zf'(z)}/{f(z)}\right)>0$ for all $z\in \mathbb{D}$. The 0-spirallike functions are the usual starlike functions. The function $f$ is parabolic starlike, if $\operatorname{Re}\!\left(\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}\right)>\left|\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}-1\right|$, and lemniscate starlike if $|(zf'(z)/f(z))^2-1|<1$ respectively. In this paper, we determine the radii of parabolic starlikeness and lemniscate starlikeness of $\alpha$-spirallike functions. Our approach combines geometric characterizations of the underlying regions with the resultant method for eliminating auxiliary variables, leading to explicit equations for the sharp radii. Some known radius results are recovered as special cases.
item.dc:creator: Lakshmipriya Arul, Vaithiyanathan Ravichandran

item.title: Unimodular random ideal hyperbolic polyhedra: geometric characteristics and random walks
item.description: arXiv:2601.14909v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We initiate a systematic study of unimodular random infinite ideal hyperbolic polyhedra in three-dimensional hyperbolic space, developing a geometric and probabilistic theory of their global behavior. At the heart of this theory is an intrinsic geometric characteristic, determined entirely by the dihedral angles surrounding a polyhedral face. We establish a unimodular Gauss-Bonnet identity and show that the expectation of this local geometric invariant completely determines the global conformal type: under suitable assumptions, a random ideal polyhedron is almost surely parabolic precisely when the expected characteristic vanishes, and hyperbolic precisely when it is negative. This provides a sharp geometric classification of random infinite ideal polyhedra. Building on the correspondence with ideal circle patterns, we further develop a refined Ring Lemma that yields quantitative geometric control without bounded-degree assumptions. Combining these geometric tools with unimodular probability methods, we identify the Poisson boundary of the face random walk and establish positive linear hyperbolic speed. Together, these results establish a local-to-global framework linking intrinsic dihedral geometry, conformal uniformization, and stochastic behavior at infinity for unimodular random infinite ideal hyperbolic polyhedra.
item.dc:creator: Huabin Ge, Yangxiang Lu, Chuwen Wang, Tian Zhou

item.title: Blaschke Conjecture and Complex Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2609.23822v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a complex-geometric approach to the Blaschke conjecture, i.e., that a manifold whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is isometric to a compact rank-one symmetric space (CROSS). In particular, we introduce the great quadric fibration, a complex analogue of the great sphere fibration. Requiring its total space to be a complex submanifold simultaneously explains many properties that a Blaschke manifold is expected to possess, including its Clifford structure, Hopf fibration, and diffeomorphism class. Furthermore, the great quadric bundle coincides with the variety of minimal rational tangents (VMRT) of the ambient Fano variety in the standard CROSS cases, and we explain this through a bend-and-break argument in the setting of the Blaschke conjecture under a suitable complexification assumption. Combining this with Hwang-Mok VMRT recognition, we prove the Blaschke conjecture for manifolds admitting an adapted complex structure on their entire tangent bundles.
item.dc:creator: Kyobeom Song

item.title: Hyperbolic area of Fatou components and new proofs of no-wandering-domain theorems
item.description: arXiv:2609.23834v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a new elementary proof of Sullivan's no-wandering-domain theorem for rational maps of degree at least two using hyperbolic area. We then develop this method further to prove that a transcendental entire function has no wandering Fatou components if its set of singular values is compact and all accumulation points of that set lie in the Fatou set. Neither proof uses quasiconformal techniques.
item.dc:creator: Zihao Ye

item.title: Failure of local extension of semipositive metrics in a smooth projective family
item.description: arXiv:2609.36410v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a smooth projective family of rational surfaces and an effective line bundle on its total space that give a negative answer to P\u{a}un's metric-extension question. The restricted bundle on the central fibre carries a semipositively curved singular Hermitian metric with analytic and minimal singularities, but this metric admits no semipositive extension to any neighbourhood of the whole fibre, even up to singularity type. The construction uses four-point blow-ups of the plane, with three centres becoming collinear on the central fibre. This change produces a nonzero integrable adjoint section on the central fibre, whereas the corresponding adjoint systems vanish on nearby noncentral fibres. If a metric extension existed, an $L^2$ extension theorem would extend that section, contradicting this vanishing.
item.dc:creator: Xiangsen Qin

item.title: Seven ordered points and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.23227v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the ordered GIT quotient of seven points on $\mathbb P^1$ with equal weights is not isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of any arithmetic complex ball quotient. Together with our companion paper and the known positive examples, this determines the equal weight case for every $n\ge6$: such a realization exists precisely for $n=6,8$. The lattice and the algebraic isomorphism are unrestricted, and torsion and divisorial ramification are allowed. The proof combines arithmetic reductions with identities involving Chern classes of fixed subvarieties and intersection inequalities for nef divisors on the GIT quotient. The final comparison includes all fixed components and requires no bound on the degree of an individual fixed curve.
item.dc:creator: Ryunosuke Nakano (Hokkaido University), Hisato Matsukawa (Hokkaido University)

item.title: Weighted configurations and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.23228v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that, for every $n\ge9$, no ordered GIT quotient of $n$ points on $\mathbb P^1$ with positive rational weights smaller than one and of total weight two is isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of an arithmetic complex ball quotient. The weights may lie on stability walls, and the lattice may have torsion and ramify along divisors. No compatibility with a prescribed period map is assumed. The proof compares homomorphisms from the tangent bundle to line bundles of negative degree with normal bundles of arithmetic fixed subvarieties. We describe these homomorphisms through coincident marked points and prove vanishing statements for their kernels. The comparison, together with integrality of Chern classes and the invariant theory of finite reflection groups, gives the nonexistence theorem without a Fano assumption on the GIT quotient.
item.dc:creator: Ryunosuke Nakano (Hokkaido University), Hisato Matsukawa (Hokkaido University)
